subject: Career
title: The Three-Paragraph Formula
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Three-Paragraph Formula usable.

hook.text: The best cover letters follow a simple structure: hook, proof, close.

buildup.text: Paragraph one: why you're excited about this specific role. Show you've done research.

discovery.text: Paragraph two: one or two achievements that directly map to the job's top needs.

twist.text: Paragraph three: a confident close that proposes next steps, not a passive 'hope to hear from you.'

climax.text: Total length: under 250 words. If it takes longer to read than a minute, it's too long.

punchline.text: Hook them, prove it, close it. Done.

quiz.question: What is the recommended structure for a cover letter?

details.summary: The three-paragraph cover letter formula structures your letter into an attention-grabbing opener, an evidence paragraph connecting your experience to the role, and a closing that requests action. This efficient structure respects the reader's time while covering all essential points.
details.whyItMatters: Long, rambling cover letters get abandoned. The three-paragraph structure ensures you communicate your value proposition completely within the typical reading window of thirty seconds.
takeaways: Paragraph one: hook the reader with a connection to their specific needs
Paragraph two: provide evidence linking your experience to the role
Paragraph three: express enthusiasm and request a specific next step

faq.question: What makes an effective opening paragraph for a cover letter?
faq.answer: Start with something specific to the company: a recent achievement, product, or challenge you want to help with. Avoid generic openers like 'I am writing to apply.' Show that you have researched the company and explain why this specific role excites you in two to three sentences.

faq.question: How long should an effective three-paragraph cover letter be in total?
faq.answer: Two hundred fifty to four hundred words is the sweet spot. This typically fills about half a page. Short enough to be read completely, long enough to communicate your key qualifications and motivation. If it extends beyond one page, it is too long regardless of quality.
